topics.title: Plotting Points with Negative Coordinates
topics.concept:
What are the 4 Quadrants?

The coordinate plane is divided into 4 quadrants by the x-axis (horizontal) and y-axis (vertical).

Quadrant II          |          Quadrant I
   (-, +)            |            (+, +)
                     |
                     |
---------------------+---------------------
                     |
                     |
Quadrant III         |          Quadrant IV
   (-, -)            |            (+, -)

Signs of Coordinates by Quadrant:

Quadrantx-coordinatey-coordinateExample
Quadrant IPositive (+)Positive (+)(3, 2)
Quadrant IINegative (-)Positive (+)(-3, 2)
Quadrant IIINegative (-)Negative (-)(-3, -2)
Quadrant IVPositive (+)Negative (-)(3, -2)

Plotting Points with Negatives:

  • Negative x → move LEFT from origin
  • Negative y → move DOWN from origin

examples.solution:
• x = -3 → move LEFT 3 units from origin
  • y = 2 → move UP 2 units
  • Plot in Quadrant II
  • Answer: Point is in Quadrant II

• x = 4 → move RIGHT 4 units
  • y = -2 → move DOWN 2 units
  • Plot in Quadrant IV
  • Answer: Point is in Quadrant IV

• x = -2 → move LEFT 2 units
  • y = -4 → move DOWN 4 units
  • Plot in Quadrant III
  • Answer: Point is in Quadrant III

• x = -5 (negative), y = 1 (positive)
  • Negative, Positive = Quadrant II
  • Answer: Quadrant II

recap: Origin (0,0) is on axes, not in any quadrant

topics.title: Finding Distance Between Points on Horizontal/Vertical Lines
topics.concept:
Finding Distance on a Coordinate Plane

When points share the same x-coordinate (vertical line) or same y-coordinate (horizontal line), distance is easy to find!

Horizontal Distance (same y-coordinate):

  • Distance = |x₂ - x₁|
  • Points move left or right only

Vertical Distance (same x-coordinate):

  • Distance = |y₂ - y₁|
  • Points move up or down only

Important: Distance is always positive (absolute value)
topics.visual:
HORIZONTAL DISTANCE (Same y):

    Points: A(-3, 2) and B(4, 2)
    
    y=2 ──────────────────────────
         ●           ●
        A(-3,2)     B(4,2)
    
    Distance = |4 - (-3)| = |4 + 3| = 7 units
    
    <───────── 7 units ─────────>


VERTICAL DISTANCE (Same x):

    Points: C(2, 5) and D(2, -3)
    
         ● C(2,5)
         │
         │
         │ 8 units
         │
         │
         ● D(2,-3)
    
    Distance = |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 units


BOTH DIRECTIONS (L-shaped path):

    From E(-2, 3) to F(4, -2)
    
    Step 1 (horizontal): from (-2,3) to (4,3)
    Distance = |4 - (-2)| = 6 units
    
    Step 2 (vertical): from (4,3) to (4,-2)
    Distance = |3 - (-2)| = 5 units
    
    Total L-shaped path = 6 + 5 = 11 units


IDENTIFYING HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL LINES:

    Horizontal line: y-coordinates are the SAME
    Vertical line:   x-coordinates are the SAME
    
    Check: (3,5) and (8,5) → same y=5 → horizontal!
    Check: (-2,4) and (-2,-7) → same x=-2 → vertical!
